body: Maresca has continued to back his first choice throughout his troubles and has no plans for in-depth conversations with his fellow Italian. “It’s much easier for me with the language,” said Maresca. “We are [having conversations] but there are players who when they make mistakes, you need conversations with them and there are players that when they make a mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises and he knows.
“With Gigio it’s quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately.

“I spoke with Gigio but sometimes you don’t need to be so deep with some players because they know they have made a mistake and recognise that. Just try to avoid that and move on. Overall he’s good. He’s quite relaxed in terms of he recognises that he has done some mistakes but at the same time he has also made some good saves.
“It’s just a matter of balance – try to avoid mistakes and continue to do the right things.”

articles.title: De Zerbi focuses on Spurs' failings - but should Bogle have seen red?
articles.summary: It was somewhat surprising to see Roberto de Zerbi take a more peaceful approach when he faced the media at Elland Road after Tottenham's 1-0 defeat by Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.
body: The Spurs manager had been expected to come out swinging in the direction of the officials after his side's first Premier League loss since September, with much of the focus falling on referee John Brooks' decision not to send Jayden Bogle off for a late challenge on Mathys Tel during the first half.
It was a decision that no doubt impacted the game - and perhaps Tottenham 's chances of earning a fourth consecutive Premier League victory for the first time since October 2023.
When Bogle caught Tel with his studs, the game was still goalless and Tottenham were arguably the team on top at Elland Road.
Following a lengthy video assistant referee (VAR) check that lasted more than four minutes, no further action was taken against the Leeds defender and the game resumed.

articles.title: Championship roundup: Stoke go top, Norwich hit five and Wrexham hold Wolves
articles.summary: Wilmot grabs winner to seal 2-1 comeback at Portsmouth. Norwich hammer Bristol City 5-0 at Ashton Gate. Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot scored as Stoke hit back to beat Portsmouth 2-1 and maintain their impressive Championship form.
body: Tyrese Shade put Portsmouth in front after six minutes with a lovely bending finish, but Stoke turned a tame first half around to make it five away wins in a row.
McGlynn capitalised on goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid’s failure to hold on to a cross before Wilmot headed home a rebound.
The result meant Stoke took top spot from Middlesbrough for at least a couple of hours, with Boro away at Watford in a 3pm kick-off. Stoke could also be displaced by Birmingham or Swansea.

“That is the first time we have won five on the bounce away from home since 1947,” said the Stoke manager, Mark Robins. “That just shows what an achievement it is. The players need to take stock of that and be proud of it. We can go into the international break satisfied and it gives us a lot to be proud of going forward.

articles.title: Manchester City break clear of Chelsea in WSL after Bronze’s freak own goal
articles.summary: Khadija Shaw hits hat-trick in City’s 5-0 rout of West Ham. Chelsea held 1-1 by Everton after Lucy Bronze own goal. body: Bronze headed ⁠the ball back across the goal to tee ​up Sandy Baltimore ‌to score ‌from close range in the 28th minute, but ‌five minutes later her attempted clearance rolled into her own net to put Everton level. The visitors held on for a draw as Chelsea dropped points for the ‌first time since the opening day of the season.

Manchester City made the most ​of that slip-up as Bunny Shaw’s superb goalscoring form continued, the Jamaican striker netting a hat-trick as her side cantered to a comprehensive win against West Ham, with Aoba ​Fujino ​and Iman Beney also on target.

The WSL’s top scorer gave City the lead six minutes before the break. City then ran riot after the interval as Shaw grabbed another couple for the match ball while Beney and Fujino scored their first goals of the campaign.

West Ham were happy to sit in and soak up the pressure from their opponents, and Constance Picaud-Inconnu was relieved when she parried Kerstin Casparij’s effort straight back into danger but no one was on hand to tap home. The visitors had the woodwork to thank for not going a goal down when Fujino’s effort hit a post.

articles.title: Taurus Bay dents some lofty reputations in Rising Stars
articles.summary: Harry Redknapp could have another top prospect on his hands after Taurus Bay made a winning chasing debut in the Boodles Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree.
body: The top guns were stumped in the Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree on Saturday as Taurus Bay made the perfect start to his chasing career with a hard-fought success over Talk To The Man.
A lot of the pre-race chatter revolved around Paul Nicholls' No Drama This End making his eagerly-awaited fences bow and he was sent off the 8-11 favourite.
However, Ben Pauling's five-year-old was a more than useful hurdler in his own right last term and always seen as more of a chasing prospect.

With No Drama This End's tank flashing empty on the run to the last it was left to Ben Jones on board Taurus Bay to outbattle the match-fit Dan Skelton runner Talk To The Man after the last, edging a one-and-a-quarter-length verdict at odds of 13-2.

articles.title: Verstappen fastest in final practice but faces grid penalties with Ferraris
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fastest in final practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix but will serve grid penalties along with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
body: Verstappen pipped new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli by 0.025s but will start at the back of the grid for a complete power unit change, while Hamilton and Leclerc have 10-grid place penalties for exceeding their internal combustion engine allocation.

Mercedes had already announced on Friday that George Russell will have a five-place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, the second time he has exceeded that part's limit, while the Ferrari drivers are being penalised for the first time, so have a bigger penalty.
It means Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris are favourites for pole position in qualifying later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5pm), live on Sky Sports F1, when rain is expected.

Norris was just 0.106s slower than Antonelli in third and also traded top spot with the Mercedes driver throughout Friday's practice sessions, as McLaren's upgrades in Brazil appear to have made an immediate performance impact.

articles.title: Rahm edges ahead of Hatton & McIlroy in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Jon Rahm leads Tyrrell Hatton and Francesca Laporta by one shot, and Rory McIlroy by two, after the third round of the Abu Dhabi Championship.
body: Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention.
The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.
Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under.
Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.

articles.title: Leeds deservedly beat Spurs after Bogle escapes red card
articles.summary: Substitute Noah Okafor’s late winner gave Leeds a 1-0 home victory over Tottenham after Whites defender Jayden Bogle controversially escaped a first-half red card.
body: Leeds were deserved victors to earn their first win in six games as Spurs saw their three-game winning run ended - but were left fuming over the Bogle decision.
The Leeds right wing-back caught Mathys Tel on his Achilles, which was awarded a foul but not punished further by referee John Brooks.
A four-minute VAR review then ensued, but Tony Harrington opted against an on-field review, with the challenge only deemed "reckless" as Tel was forced off injured as a result of it.

Ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean believed Bogle's tackle was "100 per cent a red", with the incident coming just a week after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar challenge in Spurs' win over the Eagles.

articles.title: Norwich thump five past Bristol City as home fans turn on Skubala
articles.summary: Bristol City fans turned on manager Michael Skubala as Norwich made it nine goals in successive away victories with a 5-0 Sky Bet Championship win at Ashton Gate.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Norwich at Ashton Gate on Saturday; Paris Maghoma, Harry Darling, Andre Brooks, Jovon Makama and a Mathias Kvistgaarden penalty seal a comprehensive Canaries win.

The Canaries took a 22nd-minute lead when Paris Maghoma picked up the ball 40 yards out and ran forward unchallenged before placing a low right-footed shot past Brad Collins from the left side of the box.
It was 2-0 in the 53rd minute, Jason Knight's mistimed header inside his own penalty area directing the ball to Harry Darling who coolly nodded it over Collins' despairing dive.

Three minutes later Maghoma turned provider, pulling a low cross back for Andre Brooks to fire home a third. There were still 20 minutes left when substitute Jovon Makama turned in an Anthony Musaba cross.

articles.title: Scotland lose Welsh and call up Porteous
articles.summary: Swansea City centre-back Stephen Welsh drops out the Scotland squad for their forthcoming Nations League double-header and is replaced with Los Angeles' Ryan Porteous.
body: Fears that Welsh had sustained serious knee ligament damage, following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Swansea's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth on Tuesday, appeared to have eased on Thursday.
A scan showed the 26-year-old had not suffered a significant problem and Swansea hoped he could even play some part of their game at Birmingham City on Saturday.
But the Scottish FA has now announced his withdrawal from their matches at home to North Macedonia on Friday and away to Switzerland on Monday, 16 November.
Welsh has earned all four of his caps since Sebastien Pocognoli was appointed Scotland head coach in the summer.

articles.title: Houston Texans vs. L.A. Chargers: NFL Week 9 predictions from Chronicle sports staff
articles.summary: INGLEWOOD, Calif. - The Houston Texans will face the winless Los Angles Chargers on Sunday at SoFi Stadium, one week after their off week. At 2-5, the Texans are desperate for a win in hopes of saving their season. Here are our staff predictions: Jonathan M. Alexander. Texans 23, Chargers 16.
body: The Chargers' offense is one of the worst I've seen on film, and it's largely because quarterback Justin Herbert is making poor decisions. I'll give credit to the Chargers defense for keeping most of these games close. But I think the Texans' defense finally takes advantage of Herbert's mistakes this weekend.
This version of Justin Herbert isn't the same as the Texans have seen in previous years. It's the perfect match to give Houston's defense a boost.

We've said before that losing to (fill in the blank) would be rock bottom for the Texans. This week, it's for real with the 0-7 Chargers. A loss to them would be cataclysmic for Houston and given this season, actually would be on brand. But C.J. Stroud won't let it happen in a return to his native Southern California.

The list of teams more disappointing than the Texans is a small one but the Chargers are definitely on it. Houston won't beat the doors down in Los Angeles but the defense puts in a strong performance and keeps hope alive for the coming weeks.
